**Test image key features:**
- Corn leaf with many small, circular/oval spots — tan/white/cream centers with slightly darker edges
- Scattered uniformly across the leaf surface
- Some whitish discoloration and tiny dark specks near/on the midrib
- Spots are small (~3-5mm), round, uniform

**Comparison summary:**
- **Physoderma_Brown_Spot** (ref 154): Best visual match — many small scattered yellowish-tan spots on green leaf, with dark brown spots concentrated on the midrib. Pattern and distribution are very similar to test image.
- **Eyespot** (refs 10, 25): Small circular spots scattered on leaf, but distinctly yellow/golden with dark centers — more color than test image shows.
- All other classes ruled out: rust (orange pustules), blights (elongated lesions), smuts (large galls/head involvement), viruses (streaks/mosaics), wilt diseases.

The test image matches Physoderma Brown Spot most closely: scattered small round spots on the leaf blade combined with midrib discoloration/dark lesions — the hallmark dual symptom of this disease.
